qualifying_updates.title: Grok 4.6 rolls into GitHub Copilot with admin-gated access
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced that Grok 4.6 is rolling out in GitHub Copilot for multiple IDEs, Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, and the Copilot app. The post says the model is intended for agentic coding and longer multi-step workflows, uses provider list pricing under usage-based billing, and is off by default for Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators until enabled in Copilot settings.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Model availability for coding agents is an operating-policy event, not just a product update. Teams need explicit model enablement, usage-budget review, and workflow-specific validation before allowing a new long-horizon coding model into shared agent runs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record as a governance and adoption note for model rollout gates: new model choices should require admin enablement evidence, billing awareness, and regression checks on representative agent workflows.

qualifying_updates.title: Self-hosted software-factory setup emphasizes split-plane boundaries
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Warp described a six-decision setup sequence for self-hosted software factories: orchestration ownership, execution location, outbound access, inference source, first intake-to-PR workflow, and data-exhaust storage. The guide separates execution, orchestration, model inference, and session records, and calls out worker pinning, per-role credentials, egress allowlists, retained eval data, and human fallback as explicit design choices.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent infrastructure decisions need to be documented before provisioning. The practice update reinforces split-plane architecture, egress review, scoped credentials, and one-workflow rollout as governance controls for AI-assisted development factories.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as downstream evidence for deployment-boundary checklists: local guidance should distinguish code/workspace residency, orchestration metadata, inference data, session transcripts, evals, memories, and per-role secrets.

qualifying_updates.title: CI-red coding-agent incident proposes milestone gates
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The note describes a coding agent loop that treated successful command exit codes as deployment success while CI tests were failing. It identifies a milestone-gate pattern as the fix for production-shipping coding agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent verification needs semantic checks against CI/test status, not only shell exit codes or agent self-reports. Milestone gates should assert the externally meaningful state before an agent advances to the next phase.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add to future verification coverage as evidence for milestone gates that inspect test results, deployment state, and pull-request checks rather than trusting the agent's completion narrative.

qualifying_updates.title: Planning-with-files package publishes persistent agent planning skill
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Pi lists planning-with-files version 3.10.1 as an extension and skill published on Aug 15, 2026. The package keeps task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md on disk so an agent's plan can survive context loss, compaction, clearing, crashes, and includes a security note warning that Pi packages can execute code and influence agent behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Persistent file-backed planning is becoming a reusable context architecture pattern, but package-installed skills are executable governance surfaces. Teams need source review, version pinning, and package-install risk controls before using third-party planning skills.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route to local context architecture and package-install governance: durable plans can mitigate context loss, but installable skills should be treated as code execution and instruction-surface changes.

qualifying_updates.title: Unity AI Gateway guide frames governance for agents, MCP services, and skills
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Datapao's guide describes Databricks Unity AI Gateway as a governance layer for models, agents, MCP services, skills, and tools through Unity Catalog. It highlights spend attribution, budgets, rate limits, model routing, PII and prompt-injection guardrails, request and response audit tables, action-level controls, and unified tracing for model calls and MCP tool invocations.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice signal is that AI-assisted development governance is moving from static access control toward runtime request control, cost attribution, and auditability across models, tools, and agent actions.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as a governance-and-risk routing note for control-plane patterns: evaluate whether agent tool calls, model requests, cost, approvals, guardrails, and audit trails are visible at runtime rather than only documented in policy.
